Audio Priority Bar 2.6.0 installs updates in place, files Bluetooth speakers under Speakers, and signs the app with a stable certificate. Your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Updates

- Updates now install in place through Sparkle. Once a day the app checks the latest release, verifies the archive, installs it and relaunches, waiting until the microphone is neither muted nor recording. Settings keeps a manual check and an opt-out, and an earlier opt-out carries over.
- Coming from 2.5.0, install this version once by hand or with Homebrew. Updates after it arrive in place.

## Devices

- Bluetooth speakers such as an Amazon Echo land in Speakers instead of Headphones. macOS can report a Bluetooth speaker as headphones, so from Bluetooth that claim is ignored and the device name decides. AirPods and other headphones still land in Headphones.
- A microphone that does not allow volume control says so in place of the slider, and its mute controls are disabled when it has no mute either.

## Menu bar

- The menu bar icon matches the size of the system's own items, such as Sound and Wi-Fi.
- A new option outlines the menu bar icon, to tell it apart from the system Sound item when both show the same device. It is off by default.

## Signing

- The app is signed with its own certificate instead of ad-hoc, so macOS keeps permissions you grant across updates. It is still not signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarized, so the first launch still needs Open Anyway.

Thanks to [Dave Smith](https://github.com/djsmith42) for in-place updates, the microphone volume explanation and the icon size ([#6](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/6), [#7](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/7), [#9](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/9)), and for his work on the outline option ([#11](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/11)).

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
